text:
elaine: Heads-up — noticed a weird eviction pattern on canary: leases get released but items stay in the eviction queue ~2-3s longer than expected. p50 token latency up ~12%. Sharing logs and a proposed mitigation.

raj: ugh. any obvious NACKs or retry storms in the logs? can you paste the lease release trace?

elaine: pasted a short snippet below. the lease release RPC returns OK but the downstream enqueue path sometimes gets a duplicate enqueue on retry:
```
[lease] release prefix=tenant/abc epoch=812 seq=1294 -> OK
[evict] enqueue prefix=tenant/abc token=0xdeadbeef -> ENQUEUED
[lease] release prefix=tenant/abc epoch=812 seq=1294 -> OK (retry path)
[evict] enqueue prefix=tenant/abc token=0xdeadbeef -> already-present (but no ack)
```

morgan: sounds like a race between lease callback completing and the eviction queue ack. if the enqueue path is async and the release returns earlier we may observe a window where the prefix is considered free but queue still holds it.

sasha: two quick options: 1) make lease-release wait for eviction-enqueue ack (sync path) — fixes correctness but increases tail latency on release; 2) keep async but add lease fence seq numbers + queue gating so enqueue only succeeds if seq <= current lease epoch. that needs extra metadata on queue entries.

raj: option 2 is appealing long-term. option 1 is fastest to roll out as a config flag for canary. do we have metrics to detect the false-positive enqueue case?

elaine: added two ad-hoc metrics in the canary: evict_queue_enqueue_retries and lease_release_latency_sync_path. early numbers: enqueue_retries spiked exactly when p50 went up.

morgan: tradeoffs: gating requires storing epoch/seq with each queue item and checking on dequeue. adds storage + marginal CPU on dequeue. but avoids blocking release RPCs. plus we get stronger correctness for multi-node handoff.

sasha: also need idempotency guarantees — enqueue should be idempotent by key (prefix + tag). currently it is but the ack path is leaky. we should switch to strong dedupe via a CAS on queue index or a small in-memory hash on the coordinator.

elaine: for quick mitigation I'm going to try a hybrid: make release wait up to 250ms for enqueue ack, then fall back to async and emit a debug event if timing out. that reduces release tail while fixing majority of races.

raj: SGTM. add a feature flag so we can flip per-cluster. also add a metric for release_fallback_count.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: evict-release-fallback.v1 at 2026-03-23T10:12:00Z (canary cluster 3).

morgan: long-term RFC suggestion: "Lease fences and queue gating" — include sequence math, migration strategy (backfill queue entries with epoch field), and optional GC for old epochs. we should also consider TTLs for queue entries to combat stuck items.

sasha: one more edge: tombstone handling. if a tenant tombstones a prefix right after release, gating must still allow the tombstone marker through. plan: tombstone messages carry a tombstone=true flag that bypasses fence checks but still dedupe by key.

elaine: good call. I'll include that in the quick patch and in the RFC notes.

raj: ops checklist: feature flag, metric dashboards (enqueue_retries, release_tail_p95, release_fallback_count), rollback playbook (disable flag + drain queue), postmortem trigger if p50 remains high for >10m.

elaine: will post PR with changes + smoke test plan. thanks all. :thumbsup:

morgan: nice. if quick canary looks stable we can start drafting the RFC for the gating model.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy success: evict-release-fallback.v1 (health OK).

sasha: leaving a note — we should also run a multi-tenant chaos run to simulate concurrent lease releases + handoffs. that uncovered a similar hole last quarter.

elaine: agreed. I'll schedule an end-to-end chaos test next week and tag the results here.
